**The architect's answer on the gate's queue backlog, quoted in full** (M5, 2026-10-17, `origin/main` `ba8ed63`). Posted by the PM, the card's author, as the source this card cites as "the answer". The PM re-read each file:line citation at `ba8ed63`.

> ABOUTME: Architect's answer on the Actions queue backlog behind rigger/gate and self-hosting (M5, 2026-10-17, origin/main ba8ed63).
> 
> **Recommendation: move both gate workflows to `ubuntu-latest` and skip comments on plain issues. Keep `ci.yml` on macOS.**
> 
> 1. **Nothing in the gate needs macOS.** The jobs use only bash, node, curl, openssl and tar (`.github/workflows/rigger-gate.yml:52-177`, `self-hosting.yml:52-176`). The scripts import Node built-ins and repo modules, with no platform branch (`scripts/gate-check.mjs:13-27`, `.github/scripts/self-hosting-check.mjs:10-20`). `package.json` has no dependencies and no `os` field. `D13` binds the engine's host, not CI's (`docs/spec/decisions.md:401-410`), and no R- or D-row names a runner. Only the test pins macOS: `test/workflow-files.test.mjs:242-246`.
> 2. **Narrowing comments.** The gate reads markers only from PR comments (`src/substrate/forge/read.mjs:539`). It reads acceptance from the card's body, which the `issues: edited` trigger covers (`scripts/gate-check.mjs:172-187`). So a comment on a plain issue changes nothing. Add `if: github.event_name != 'issue_comment' || github.event.issue.pull_request` to each `card` job. Filtering on the `rigger-marker` fence would also be sound (`ARCHITECTURE.md:304`), but an edit needs `changes.body.from` too. That is more fragile, so leave it out for now.
> 3. **`ci.yml` stays on macOS.** The suite and the demo exercise the engine on its host (`ci.yml:17`, `D13`).
> 4. **Files:** the two workflows, `templates/github/workflows/rigger-gate.yml` and `test/workflow-files.test.mjs`. All but the test are Self-hosting paths (`AGENTS.md:202-204`). So the card needs a sound owner marker, and the engine never dispatches it (`D25` rules 5 and 7). No binding-document delta is needed. The template ships to consumers, but README:193 describes the engine's host, so it stays true.

**PM (author): announcing edits to this card, under `R-CARD-5`, for the owner's ruling [P71](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/642#issuecomment-6235632446) and the architect's answer on Node.** I read the image list myself at `06f4a9146f`: `ubuntu-latest` defaults to Node.js 22.23.3, and its tool cache holds 24.21.0.

- Item 1's "stop if below 24" is replaced by the fix: a step that puts the tool cache's Node 24 first on `PATH`, shown by a test. A new item 2 keeps the Node floor check exactly as it is.
- The workflow-diff item admits that step and nothing else.
- The grant class extends to the test lines at 249–260 and 475, keeping each assertion on the Node check.
- A new Close-out entry has the first Ubuntu runs log `node v24.*`.
- "As P69 set for #665" becomes P71.

No item is weakened. Each edit gives the text it replaces and the text that replaces it, exactly as the body will read. The acceptance then holds 17 items, and Close-out 7 entries.

**1. Citations: P71.**

Replaces:

> and [P69](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/642#issuecomment-6228218874), whose close-out reader this card adopts.

With:

> [P69](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/642#issuecomment-6228218874), and [P71](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/642#issuecomment-6235632446), which gives this card P69's close-out reader.
> - The `ubuntu-latest` image's [software list](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/06f4a9146f/images/ubuntu/Ubuntu2404-Readme.md) at `actions/runner-images` commit `06f4a9146f` (image 20261012.334.1), cited as "the image list".

**2. Grant classes: the Node-step test lines.**

Replaces:

> keeping the workflows it reads. No other existing line under `test/` is covered.

With:

> keeping the workflows it reads. In the same file, the Node-check test at lines 249–260 and the step check at line 475 may admit the tool-cache step: they may count it among a job's steps and place it before "Check the Node version", keeping every assertion on that check's place before the script, its run text, and its outcome for each Node version it tries. No other existing line under `test/` is covered.

**3. Rests on: P71.**

Replaces:

> - **Rests on:** P34, P35, P69;

With:

> - **Rests on:** P34, P35, P69, P71;

**4. Why: the Node default on Ubuntu.**

Replaces:

> Nothing in either gate workflow needs macOS (the answer, point 1), provided the Ubuntu runner's own Node meets the workflows' `NODE_MAJOR`, which the acceptance checks first.

With:

> Nothing in either gate workflow needs macOS (the answer, point 1), but Node. Both workflows refuse a runner whose Node is below `NODE_MAJOR`, `'24'` at `ba8ed63`, and they install no Node, since no step may have a `uses:` (`test/workflow-files.test.mjs`). The image list gives `ubuntu-latest`'s default Node as 22.23.3 (line 26), and its tool cache holds 24.21.0 (Cached Tools, Node.js). So each job puts the tool cache's Node 24 first on its `PATH` before the version check, which still refuses a Node below 24.

**5. Item 1: the tool-cache step replaces the Node-default stop.**

Replaces:

> - Before any workflow change, the pull request quotes the Node.js version that GitHub's runner-images repository documents as the default on `ubuntu-latest`, with the document's URL and commit, and its major is at least the `NODE_MAJOR` both gate workflows name (`'24'` at `ba8ed63`). Where it is below, the maker stops and returns the card to the PM, because both workflows fail a run on a runner whose Node is below `NODE_MAJOR` and install no Node of their own.

With:

> - In each job of `.github/workflows/rigger-gate.yml`, `templates/github/workflows/rigger-gate.yml` and `.github/workflows/self-hosting.yml`, a step before "Check the Node version" puts the newest `${RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE}/node/24.*/x64/bin` first on `GITHUB_PATH`, with no `uses:` and no download, shown by a test that runs the step against a fake tool cache holding more than one Node 24 and a Node 22.
> - The "Check the Node version" step in each of those jobs keeps its base text, so a run still fails on a Node below `NODE_MAJOR`, shown by `git diff` against the base changing none of that step's lines.

**6. Item 5 (item 4 before this edit): the workflow diff admits the tool-cache step.**

Replaces:

> `git diff` against the base changes only `runs-on` lines and adds only the `card` job's condition line.

With:

> `git diff` against the base changes only `runs-on` lines, and adds only the `card` job's condition line and each job's tool-cache step.

**7. Close-out: P71.**

Replaces:

> and posts its verdict on this card, as P69 set for #665.

With:

> and posts its verdict on this card (P71).

**8. Close-out: a new first entry, the Node the first runs log.**

Replaces:

> - Every job of the first `rigger-gate` run and the first `self-hosting` run that start after the merge ran on an `ubuntu-latest` runner, shown by a read of each run's jobs and their labels.

With:

> - Every job of the first `rigger-gate` run and the first `self-hosting` run that start after the merge ran on an `ubuntu-latest` runner, shown by a read of each run's jobs and their labels.
> - Each of those jobs logs `node v24.` followed by its minor and patch in its "Check the Node version" step, quoted from its log.

The line:

Post-merge close-out probe for #794: this is a comment on the plain issue. The rigger-gate and self-hosting card jobs should be skipped, with no runner assigned.

**#794 post-merge close-out record.** PR #797 merged 2026-10-18T14:32:21Z as `2eb21673be87e57fe13a3d3fa73f34c4e300b692` (PR merge field and the PM's post-merge body line). This is the one record for P71's independent Claude reviewer.

1. **First workflow runs after merge.**

   > Every job of the first `rigger-gate` run and the first `self-hosting` run that start after the merge ran on an `ubuntu-latest` runner, shown by a read of each run's jobs and their labels.

   The first `rigger-gate` run was [39136470624](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39136470624), and the first `self-hosting` run was [39136470547](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39136470547), both `issue_comment` at 14:32:41Z after the coordinator's 14:32:39Z reopen comment. Each had two `skipped` jobs; each job declared label `ubuntu-latest`, but `runner_name` was null. They did not run on a runner. The first runs with executed jobs were the PM body-edit `issues` runs [39136516990](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39136516990) and [39136516823](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39136516823) at 14:33:17Z. Their four jobs succeeded with `labels: ["ubuntu-latest"]` and non-null `runner_name` values. **Unmet under the current wording (`ambiguous`).** The first pair cannot show jobs that ran on Ubuntu. The card's author must say whether its intended scope was the first runs with executed jobs; the independent reviewer must rule on the record.

2. **Node in those jobs.**

   > Each of those jobs logs `node v24.` followed by its minor and patch in its "Check the Node version" step, quoted from its log.

   The first skipped pair has no "Check the Node version" logs. In the first executed pair, each job’s “Check the Node version” log says `node v24.21.0; this workflow names Node 24`: gate [Resolve the card, 117702010158](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39136516990/job/117702010158) and [Rule and post, 117702038135](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39136516990/job/117702038135); self-hosting [Resolve the card, 117702009594](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39136516823/job/117702009594) and [Check and post, 117702029921](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39136516823/job/117702029921). **Unmet under the current wording (`ambiguous`).** The first pair cannot show Node logs. This is the same scope question as entry 1.

3. **Maker's plain-issue comment.**

   > A comment the maker posts on this card after the merge raises `rigger-gate` and `self-hosting` runs whose every job is skipped and none is assigned a runner, shown by a read of those runs' jobs.

   [Comment 6251130157](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/794#issuecomment-6251130157) was created at 14:33:13Z. Another plain-issue comment, the PM's edit announcement, was created in the same second. The resulting `issue_comment` runs at 14:33:16Z were gate [39136515750](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39136515750) and [39136515751](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39136515751), and self-hosting [39136515532](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39136515532) and [39136515777](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39136515777). Every job in all four runs concluded `skipped` with `runner_name: null`. Because the two same-second comments cannot be mapped individually to run IDs from the run metadata, the set proves the maker comment raised one all-skipped run of each workflow.

4. **Maker's PR comment.**

   > A comment the maker posts on this card's pull request after the merge raises a `rigger-gate` run and a `self-hosting` run whose `card` job runs on `ubuntu-latest`, shown by a read of their jobs.

   [Comment 6251130854](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/pull/797#issuecomment-6251130854) was created at 14:33:17Z after merge. Gate run [39136520809](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39136520809) and self-hosting run [39136520769](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39136520769) started at 14:33:20Z. Their `Resolve the card` jobs succeeded with `labels: ["ubuntu-latest"]` and non-null GitHub Actions runner names. Both posting jobs also succeeded on Ubuntu.

5. **PM's body edit.**

   > An edit the card's author makes to this card's body after the merge, at the maker's request and outside the acceptance, raises a `rigger-gate` run and a `self-hosting` run whose `card` job runs on `ubuntu-latest`, shown by a read of their jobs.

   The PM [announced the edit](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/794#issuecomment-6251130095) at 14:33:13Z and the #794 body now cites merge commit `2eb2167` outside acceptance (`updated_at: 14:33:14Z`). The resulting `issues` runs at 14:33:17Z were [39136516990](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39136516990) and [39136516823](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39136516823). Their `Resolve the card` jobs succeeded with `labels: ["ubuntu-latest"]` and non-null runner names. Both posting jobs also succeeded on Ubuntu.

6. **First status on an open PR from Ubuntu runs.**

   > The first `rigger/gate` and `self-hosting` statuses that an `ubuntu-latest` run posts on an open pull request are posted by `rigger-gate[bot]` on the head that run's log names, quoted.

   The first qualifying open-PR pair is #792: [gate run 39137975171](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39137975171) and [self-hosting run 39137975172](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39137975172), both `pull_request_target` at 14:52:55Z, all jobs successful with `labels: ["ubuntu-latest"]` and non-null runner names. #792 was `OPEN` at both status times and remained open at the read; its head was `a2b556c976a6128d3ca0b2a3afcfa7bde3961125`. Gate [posting job 117706321452](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39137975171/job/117706321452) log names `head: a2b556c976a6128d3ca0b2a3afcfa7bde3961125` and `posted {"state":"failure","context":"rigger/gate","description":"reviewer: no marker"} on a2b556c976a6128d3ca0b2a3afcfa7bde3961125`; the [commit status](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/commit/a2b556c976a6128d3ca0b2a3afcfa7bde3961125) was created at 14:53:17Z by `rigger-gate[bot]`. Self-hosting [posting job 117706325690](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/actions/runs/39137975172/job/117706325690) log names the same head and `posted {"state":"failure","context":"self-hosting","description":"owner: no marker"} on` it; the commit status was created at 14:53:15Z by `rigger-gate[bot]`. The refusal reasons reflect #792's missing markers. The earlier executed post-merge runs concerned merged #797 or new issues #800–803; the other earlier issue-comment runs skipped. The complete `gh run list --created ">=2026-10-18T14:32:21Z"` inventory through 14:52:55Z had no other open-PR run.

7. **Queue before and one hour after merge.**

   > The record quotes `gh run list --status queued` taken before the merge, and again one hour after it, each counted by workflow.

   The card's measured `gh run list --status queued` reading at 2026-10-17T15:11Z (before merge) was 16: six `rigger-gate`, six `self-hosting`, four CI. At exactly 2026-10-18T15:32:21Z (one hour after merge), `gh run list -R williacj/rigger --status queued --limit 1000 --json databaseId,workflowName,name,createdAt,status` returned two queued runs: one `rigger-gate` (39140936313) and one `self-hosting` (39140936280), zero CI. The saved unfiltered JSON and command output agree.

**Close-out assessment:** entries 3–7 met; entries 1–2 unmet on the current literal wording (`ambiguous`). The first runs after merge were the skipped runs raised by the coordinator’s reopen comment. I need the card author’s decision on whether “first” may mean first runs with executed jobs; then a fresh independent Claude `reviewer` must rule under P71. The card stays open.

**PM (author): announcing an edit to Close-out entry 1, under `R-CARD-5`, answering the scope question in the [close-out record](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/794#issuecomment-6251729533).** Only entry 1's text changes. Entry 2 keeps its text, and its "those jobs" now refers to the runs the revised entry 1 names. No acceptance item and no other entry changes.

**Ruling: this keeps the entries' intent and is not a weakening.** Entries 1 and 2 test that the first jobs to execute after the merge get an `ubuntu-latest` runner and Node 24. A job that is skipped never gets a runner and never runs a step, so it can show neither. Skipped runs are the subject of Close-out entry 3, and the card's own condition skips them by design. "First" still names exactly one run of each workflow, so the maker gets no choice among runs, and "every job" still holds. I read the runs myself:

- The first runs after the merge were `rigger-gate` 39136470624 and `self-hosting` 39136470547 (`issue_comment`, 14:32:41Z). Every job was `skipped`, `runner_name` null.
- Every run between them and the next pair was also `issue_comment` and all-skipped (39136515532, 39136515750, 39136515751, 39136515777, all 14:33:16Z).
- The first runs with executed jobs are `rigger-gate` 39136516990 and `self-hosting` 39136516823 (`issues`, 14:33:17Z). All four jobs are `success`, with `labels: ["ubuntu-latest"]` and non-null runner names. Each "Check the Node version" step logs `node v24.21.0; this workflow names Node 24`.

So no executed run is skipped over.

**Close-out entry 1.**

Replaces:

> - Every job of the first `rigger-gate` run and the first `self-hosting` run that start after the merge ran on an `ubuntu-latest` runner, shown by a read of each run's jobs and their labels.

With:

> - Every job of the first `rigger-gate` run and the first `self-hosting` run that start after the merge with a job that is not skipped ran on an `ubuntu-latest` runner, shown by a read of each run's jobs, their labels and their runner names. A run whose every job is skipped is not one of these runs. The comment entry below covers such runs.

**Claude reviewer — #794 close-out (P71), acceptance 5ea30ee5597a: sound**

**What I reviewed.** The maker's [close-out record](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/794#issuecomment-6251729533), checked against the card's current Close-out. The body digest is `5ea30ee5597aa2649dfc0d37eb9f54a90cc1932a40bbe490c01d147ee98ae351`, from `sha256` of `gh issue view 794 --json body -q .body`. That body carries the PM's revised entry 1 ([announcement](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/794#issuecomment-6253348529), after [C57](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/642#issuecomment-6251895395)). PR #797 merged at 2026-10-18T14:32:21Z as `2eb21673be87e57fe13a3d3fa73f34c4e300b692` (`gh pr view 797`), and it is an ancestor of `main` at `62eeb1d`. The record quotes entry 1's earlier wording, so I ruled its evidence against the current text. Every read below is mine, made read-only through `gh api`.

**Run inventory.** I listed every run created between 14:30Z and 14:55Z (`actions/runs?created=…`). Between the merge and the first executed pair, the only runs were CI push 39136450389 and the all-skipped `issue_comment` runs 39136470624, 39136470547, 39136515532, 39136515750, 39136515751 and 39136515777.

1. **Met.** Entry: "Every job of the first `rigger-gate` run and the first `self-hosting` run that start after the merge with a job that is not skipped ran on an `ubuntu-latest` runner, shown by a read of each run's jobs, their labels and their runner names. …"
   - The first such `rigger-gate` run is 39136516990 (`issues`, 14:33:17Z). Its jobs are 117702010158 "Resolve the card" (`GitHub Actions 1000021523`) and 117702038135 "Rule and post" (`GitHub Actions 1000021527`).
   - The first such `self-hosting` run is 39136516823. Its jobs are 117702009594 (`GitHub Actions 1000021522`) and 117702029921 (`GitHub Actions 1000021526`).
   - All four jobs succeeded with `labels: ubuntu-latest`. Each "Set up job" log reads `Image: ubuntu-24.04`, `Version: 20261012.334.1`.
2. **Met.** Entry: "Each of those jobs logs `node v24.` followed by its minor and patch in its "Check the Node version" step, quoted from its log." In all four job logs, the step that runs `running="$(node --version)"` (named "Check the Node version" at `.github/workflows/rigger-gate.yml:67` and `:123`) logs `node v24.21.0; this workflow names Node 24`.
3. **Met.** Entry: "A comment the maker posts on this card after the merge raises `rigger-gate` and `self-hosting` runs whose every job is skipped and none is assigned a runner …" [Comment 6251130157](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/794#issuecomment-6251130157) is from 14:33:13Z. Its runs are among 39136515750, 39136515751, 39136515532 and 39136515777, and every job in all four is `skipped` with `runner_name` null. The second comment posted in the same second cannot be told apart from it, but that does not affect the ruling, because every run of both comments skipped.
4. **Met.** Entry: "A comment the maker posts on this card's pull request after the merge raises a `rigger-gate` run and a `self-hosting` run whose `card` job runs on `ubuntu-latest` …" [Comment 6251130854](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/pull/797#issuecomment-6251130854) is from 14:33:17Z.
   - Run 39136520809 "Resolve the card" (job `card`) ran on `ubuntu-latest`, `GitHub Actions 1000021525`, and succeeded.
   - Run 39136520769 ran on `ubuntu-latest`, `GitHub Actions 1000021524`, and succeeded.
5. **Met.** Entry: "An edit the card's author makes to this card's body after the merge … raises a `rigger-gate` run and a `self-hosting` run whose `card` job runs on `ubuntu-latest` …" The PM's announced citation-line edit is outside the acceptance and present in the current body. It raised the `issues` runs 39136516990 and 39136516823, whose `card` jobs ran on `ubuntu-latest` (entry 1 above).
6. **Met.** Entry: "The first `rigger/gate` and `self-hosting` statuses that an `ubuntu-latest` run posts on an open pull request are posted by `rigger-gate[bot]` on the head that run's log names, quoted."
   - **Earlier executed runs.** Every posting job before 14:52:55Z made no post on an open PR. The #794 and #800–#803 runs log "has no open pull request … so nothing is posted". The #797-comment runs posted on `87d9218…` with "pull request #797 is merged, not open".
   - **Gate run.** Run 39137975171 (#792, open, head `a2b556c976a6128d3ca0b2a3afcfa7bde3961125`), job 117706321452, logs `head: a2b556c…` and `posted {"state":"failure","context":"rigger/gate","description":"reviewer: no marker"} on a2b556c976a6128d3ca0b2a3afcfa7bde3961125`.
   - **Self-hosting run.** Run 39137975172, job 117706325690, logs the same head and `posted {"state":"failure","context":"self-hosting","description":"owner: no marker"} on a2b556c…`.
   - **Statuses on the head.** `commits/a2b556c…/statuses` lists the earliest pair as `rigger-gate[bot]`, `rigger/gate` at 14:53:17Z and `self-hosting` at 14:53:15Z.
7. **Met.** Entry: "The record quotes `gh run list --status queued` taken before the merge, and again one hour after it, each counted by workflow."
   - **Before the merge.** The record quotes the card's measured reading at 2026-10-17T15:11Z: 6 / 6 / 4.
   - **One hour after.** At 15:32:21Z the record reports one `rigger-gate` run (39140936313), one `self-hosting` run (39140936280) and 0 CI.
   - **My check of the hour reading.** Both runs were created at 15:32:20Z and their first jobs started at 15:32:22Z. No other run that day, CI included, had a non-skipped job starting after 15:32:21Z.

**Coverage.** The record answers all seven entries and cites the runs, jobs and comments each one needs. It predates the entry 1 revision, but its own evidence (the executed pair, their labels and non-null runner names) is what the revised entry asks for. I found nothing in the Close-out that falls short of what the card asked: it tests the runner, Node, both comment paths, the body-edit path, the first open-PR status, and the queue.

**Blocking findings.** None.

**Non-blocking.** I rebuilt the 2026-10-17 pre-merge queue after the fact, from job start times. It gives about 15 runs (6 `rigger-gate`, 6 `self-hosting`, 3 CI) rather than 16. That method cannot see run-level `queued` status exactly, and re-runs reset job start times, so I do not treat it as contradicting the card's live reading. Entry 7 asks the record to quote a reading, and it does.

**Verification.** Every check was a read-only `gh api` call: `actions/runs?created=…`, `actions/runs/<id>/jobs`, `actions/jobs/<id>/logs`, `commits/<sha>/statuses`, `issues/<n>/comments`, plus `gh pr view 797` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor`. I ran no test suite and no Rigger.

**Verdict: sound.** All seven Close-out entries are met at acceptance digest `5ea30ee5597a`.
Closing on the P71 close-out verdict, sound at acceptance 5ea30ee5597a: https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/794#issuecomment-6253444992. — M5 coordinator
